Also available at: http:// www.cdc.gov/mmwr/PDF/rr/rr5108.pdf (accessed 21/06/05) Infections in immunocompromised patients Immunocompromised patients are at increased risk of in- fections, including those caused by fungi. Fungi most commonly affecting AIDS patients include Cryptococcus neoformans, Pneumocystis jirovecii and Candida albicans while those associated with immunosuppressive therapy and cancer are mainly Aspergillus and Candida spp. Im- munocompromised patients are also at increased risk of endemic mycoses, such as coccidioidomycosis, histoplas- mosis, and Penicillium marneffei as well as a growing number of uncommon fungi reported to cause invasive in- fections, including Fusarium, Scedosporium, and Trichos- poron species. Fungal infections in immunocompromised patients are of- ten invasive or disseminated and treatment should start as early as possible. A fungal cause of infection should be considered in patients with persistent febrile neutropenia
